extracted.intended_audience: PhD students and early-career researchers who are or will be serving as peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for PhD students on how to perform constructive, professional peer reviews of manuscripts. Emphasizes scope of feedback, tone, leveraging expertise, learning benefits, and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't try to change everything about the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on constructive feedback rather than rewriting. "Only point out issues if they are grammatically wrong, poorly structured, or illogical." Don't impose your style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on substantive problems (grammar, structure, logic) instead of re-authoring the manuscript; avoid substituting your stylistic preferences for the author's voice. Prioritize high-impact, clear corrections over exhaustive line edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider your supervisor's approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect on the kind of feedback you've valued from mentors; balance critique with encouragement; respect the author's voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mentoring styles that have helped you as a model—provide constructive, balanced comments that both point out issues and acknowledge strengths. Be mindful not to enforce your supervisor's exact style; contextualize suggestions rather than dictating changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an "expert" mentality
rubrics_metrics.description: "You know more than you think. Embrace your expertise." Your specialized knowledge from years of study has value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be confident in contributing subject-matter insights. Do not undercut your authority by over-apologizing; offer evidence-based critiques and identify gaps or mistakes within your expertise while signaling uncertainties where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviews to reinforce your own learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat peer review as an opportunity to apply your training; ask the same critical questions you'd ask of your own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach reviewing as a learning exercise—practicing evaluation sharpens your own research and writing. Reflect on methodological, conceptual, and presentation issues as you would for your manuscripts, and internalize lessons for future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the positives
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance criticism with strengths. Use respectful language like "This section would benefit from…" rather than harsh feedback. Stay objective; avoid personal attacks; complete reviews within 3–4 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques constructively and cite specific examples of strengths as well as weaknesses. Use professional, non-personal phrasing and retain objectivity. Observe expected reviewer timeliness (aim to complete reviews in about 3–4 weeks).
